html:
Tewodros II was emperor of Ethiopia from 1855 until 1868, a provincial warlord who reunited the country after the long Era of the Princes, when emperors were puppets of regional lords.

Born Kassa Hailu, he fought his way to the throne and was crowned in 1855. He tried to build a national army, curb the church and the nobles, and make cannon with the help of European missionaries.

His rule turned violent as revolts spread. When he jailed the British consul and other Europeans, Britain sent an army from India, which stormed his fortress of Magdala in April 1868, and he shot himself rather than be taken. His dream of a strong unified state was carried on by Yohannes IV and Menelik II, and he is remembered as a national hero in Ethiopia.
